chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jameela, from Abdillah ibn Sulayman, from Abdillah ibn Abu Ja'far, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) [that he said]:

Regarding the eye of the one-eyed person, which was firm (functional), then it became blurred (lost function). So he (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) had judged with regards to it being half the wergild for the healthy eye.

key_terms.الْعَيْنِ الْعَوْرَاءِ: The one-eyed person (literally: the eye of the blind)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation (diya) for injuring the remaining eye of a one-eyed person?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of proportional compensation (*diya*) for injury to the remaining functional eye of a one-eyed person, ruling it at half the value of a healthy eye. Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and rooted in the judgment of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), it illustrates the Shia jurisprudential approach to calculating damages based on the loss of specific utility rather than a flat rate. This ruling underscores the precision of early Imamic legal reasoning in personal injury cases.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Abu Jameela, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, from Abdullah Bin Abu Ja’far,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the eye of the one-eyed which was firm, then it blurred out. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> had judged with regards to it being half the wergild for the healthy eye’.
